{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.5,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D30", "R60", "R59", "U36"],
      "pins": ["D30.4", "D30.2", "D30.3", "R60.2"],
      "nets": ["ESTOP_OUT", "/LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV"],
      "observed": "The anode A2 (pin 4) of the dual LED D30 is on ESTOP_OUT, the same net that R60 returns to. Its cathode K2 (pin 2) is in series through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT. That loop has no supply, so the second LED can never conduct. The other LED in D30 (A1, pin 3) is correctly on the LED supply net /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV. Every other indicator LED in the design (D8, D28, D29) has its anode on that supply net and its cathode driven through a 130 Ω resistor to a signal.",
      "expected": "D30 pin 4 (A2) should sit on the LED supply /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV like its sibling A1. ESTOP_OUT should only be the sink side through R60, so the E-stop indicator lights when the line is pulled low.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"A1\") (pintype \"input\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The E-stop indicator LED from D30 never lights, so operators lose a status indication on the e-stop output line.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R36"],
      "pins": ["R36.1", "R36.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R36 is valued 24k, but its sourced part is a 24 Ω resistor. The LCSC description reads 24Ω and the MPN FRC0805J240TSD encodes 24 Ω.",
      "expected": "A 24 kΩ, 125 mW part across the 28 V-class output, as the schematic value implies, to keep dissipation within rating. The BOM part must match the value.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R36\") (value \"24k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24 Ω part is populated, it would dissipate tens of watts across the high-voltage output and fail, or it could load the output heavily.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D4", "D14", "D23"],
      "pins": ["D4.2", "D14.2", "D23.2"],
      "nets": ["/LED_3.3V_POWER_SW"],
      "observed": "The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW has only the anodes of D4, D14 and D23 and no driver, switch, jumper or supply connected to it.",
      "expected": "A switched LED supply feeding these activity and link LEDs, since their cathodes are driven through R10, R2 and R3.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"32\") (name \"/LED_3.3V_POWER_SW\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D14\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The Ethernet link/activity and CM4 activity indicators can never light.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The clearest deviation is in the E-stop indicator: D30's second LED anode (A2) is tied to ESTOP_OUT rather than the LED supply that its sibling uses, so that LED cannot conduct. Two lower-confidence items are a 24 kΩ value whose sourced part is 24 Ω, and an undriven LED supply net feeding three indicator LEDs."
}

anomalies.observed: The anode A2 (pin 4) of the dual LED D30 is on ESTOP_OUT, the same net that R60 returns to. Its cathode K2 (pin 2) is in series through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT. That loop has no supply, so the second LED can never conduct. The other LED in D30 (A1, pin 3) is correctly on the LED supply net /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV. Every other indicator LED in the design (D8, D28, D29) has its anode on that supply net and its cathode driven through a 130 Ω resistor to a signal.
anomalies.expected: D30 pin 4 (A2) should sit on the LED supply /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV like its sibling A1. ESTOP_OUT should only be the sink side through R60, so the E-stop indicator lights when the line is pulled low.
anomalies.impact: The E-stop indicator LED from D30 never lights, so operators lose a status indication on the e-stop output line.

anomalies.observed: R36 is valued 24k, but its sourced part is a 24 Ω resistor. The LCSC description reads 24Ω and the MPN FRC0805J240TSD encodes 24 Ω.
anomalies.expected: A 24 kΩ, 125 mW part across the 28 V-class output, as the schematic value implies, to keep dissipation within rating. The BOM part must match the value.
anomalies.impact: If the 24 Ω part is populated, it would dissipate tens of watts across the high-voltage output and fail, or it could load the output heavily.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW has only the anodes of D4, D14 and D23 and no driver, switch, jumper or supply connected to it.
anomalies.expected: A switched LED supply feeding these activity and link LEDs, since their cathodes are driven through R10, R2 and R3.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet link/activity and CM4 activity indicators can never light.
